channel.title: Thoughts by Your Hommie
channel.description: Statistical and machine learning cases, simulations that verify beliefs before the data arrives, and stats textbooks rewritten simpler.

item.title: Which Nigerian states got worse, and their deadliest months
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: Thirty-three of thirty-seven states got worse between 2015 and 2025, at speeds from 1.5 to 59.8 per cent a year. Borno, one death in three, barely moved. Rank by speed and rank by size are different lists.

item.title: How big should the spoon be?
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: Five hundred interviews from the whole register named Nigeria’s winner 3,967 times in 4,000. Forty thousand from phone owners named it never. El-Rufai had the right objection and quoted the wrong one.

item.title: The standard error, derived in three lines
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: Casella and Berger reach the standard error through variance algebra, before any sampling distribution exists. The repeated-samples story that most introductions lead with is an interpretation of that line, not a way to get it.
